svg.title: What the failover test does
svg.desc: A real Flink high-availability cluster runs in Docker with ZooKeeper, three JobManagers, two TaskManagers and a shared storage which rejects expired tokens. Tokens expire after 30 seconds. A leader renews its token every 15 seconds, a standby JobManager of an unfixed Flink never does. The test kills the leader. Without the fix the new leader reads the storage with an expired token, the call is rejected and the JobManager dies. With the fix its token is fresh and the job recovers. The driver asserts on stale tokens, rejected calls, fatal errors, unexpected exits, renewal cadence and timeouts.
svg.text: Does the next JobManager still have a valid token?
A real Flink HA cluster in Docker, tokens that really expire, and a leader that gets killed.

g.text: All five processes use the storage,
for HA data and checkpoints. It rejects
every call that has an expired token.
new token every 15 s, sent to the TMs
Every token lives 30 s. Each JobManager
should renew its own every 15 s.
It reads the HA storage with its own token:
jm2 dies with a fatal error.
The driver kills the leader after every
standby has outlived two token lifetimes.

svg.text: Then the driver checks recorded facts, nothing is assumed
a process died on its own
too few or too many token
